maya: heads-up — seeing a reproducible MRR drop when we compare new-reranker-v3 fp16 -> int8 on the short-query slice (<=3 tokens).
maya: quick numbers from eval harness (same candidates, same seed):
maya: ```
model         NDCG@10   MRR
new-reranker-v3-fp16  0.367     0.312
new-reranker-v3-int8  0.364     0.295
delta                      -0.003    -0.017
```
maya: delta MRR -0.017 looks small but it's concentrated on very short queries and the confidence intervals don't overlap.
eli: can you paste the CI method? bootstrap? how many reps?
maya: bootstrap 10k reps, stratified by query length bucket. 95% CI for MRR fp16: [0.306,0.318], int8: [0.287,0.303]. p-value ~ 0.004 (two-sided).
ci-bot: perf-checker: bootstrap p=0.0041 (10k reps). flagged: regression short-query MRR.
alex: interesting. any difference in tokenization between the two builds? were we using different tokenizer versions during quant eval?
maya: checked tokenizer artifacts — same tokenizer binary. but candidate ordering was slightly different because of dedupe step upstream (we re-ran candidates with shuffling turned off for fp16 run, accidentally left shuffle on for int8 run).
eli: that could explain some noise but not systematic drop concentrated on short queries, right? if candidate order changed, MRR should be noisy both directions.
sam: product perspective — short queries are 22% of traffic for our search product. a 1.7pt MRR hit on that slice might be noticeable for user metrics. :eyes:
alex: maybe quantization induced stronger calibration shift for very short contexts — fewer tokens means the model relies more on embeddings/cosine margin; quant errors could move ranks for near-ties.
maya: agreed. hypothesis list: 1) candidate ordering artifact 2) tokenizer/truncation edgecases for empty-ish docs 3) quantization calibration shift (score scale) 4) evaluation harness metric bug for ties.
eli: let's do lightweight checks in parallel:
eli: - reproduce runs with identical candidate ordering (seeded)
eli: - compute pairwise swap rate for top-5 between fp16 and int8 on short queries
eli: - compute score distribution shift (mean/std) per rank for short queries
eli: - run tie-handling deterministic metric (averaged tie-break)
maya: I can repro with seeded candidates now. starting a job: eval-job/new-rerank-int8-seeded-shortquery (ETA ~ 45m).
ci-bot: infra: started eval job eval-job/44981 at 1719876600 by maya.
alex: also run a small quant-aware calibration (temp scaling) to see if multiplicative scaling eliminates delta. i can throw up a quick script.
maya: done quick prod-like calibration on a 5k dev subset: applying scalar 0.98 to int8 scores brings MRR to 0.309 (within CI).
eli: that points to a calibration/scale effect, but we should still figure out why scale changed after int8. could be kernel-level bias or fused layer reorder.
sam: actionable ask: if calibration fix is stable, can we ship int8 with post-calibration as interim? what's the perf/cost tradeoff?
alex: cost/perf: int8 gives ~1.9x throughput, latency improves ~20–30% p50, cost down ~38%. calibration is just a cheap scalar at serving time.
maya: plan: 1) finish seeded run and swap-rate analysis (me) 2) eli to run tied-metric and per-rank score histograms 3) alex to instrument kernel-level score diff traces on a tiny sample 4) if all point to scale, we test scalar calibration in staged rollout canary (10% traffic)
eli: also let's add bootstrap for swap-rate (confidence on swap fraction) and per-query delta histogram, to avoid cherry-picking.
maya: agreed. will post results in this thread when job finishes.
ci-bot: eval-job/44981 completed at 1719877000. artifacts: s3://redwood-eval/new-rerank-int8-seeded-shortquery/44981/results.tar.gz
maya: seeded-run numbers: fp16 MRR 0.313, int8 0.294 delta -0.019. swap-rate (top5) = 12.4% (bootstrap 95% CI [11.1,13.7]).
eli: swap-rate seems high but consistent with the MRR shift. how many near-tie candidates?
maya: ~18% of short-query cases have top-3 scores within 0.02 margin.
alex: that small margin is right in quant noise territory. I still want kernel trace but this is already pretty indicative.
sam: pragmatic move: roll scalar calibration in canary and measure CTR/engagement on short-query traffic slice. if no regression we can proceed.
maya: I'll run canary simulation (offline) applying scalar 0.98 then run holdout A/B on replay traffic. ETA 2 days.
eli: and add unit test in eval harness to assert that score mean shift after quantization must be < 0.01 else fail onboarding.
maya: noted. i'll open a tiny PR to add shift check to the onboarding checklist.
sam: thanks all. keep updates here. :thumbsup:
